mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which compresses earnings and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, increasing real discount rates and eroding real earnings, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of dual-shock episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 6-month averages signals robust household demand, which predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months, combined with rising average hourly earnings (not directly observed but implied by labor market tightness), signals a late-cycle labor market overheating, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to earnings pressure and recession risk.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
